subfamily: rum and Coca-Cola with lime (the Codex's Cuba Libre build), Angostura bitters on top
glass: tall glass (highball, about 350 ml), filled with ice
_status: v1 (Tomas, round 3; notes r5: S1 rum-making 1930s, TDL 1949; S2 white rum and three cubes in the Codex, aged rum and a full glass of ice are mine; S3 after Baker's way, without his muddling; 1919 at 40% unconfirmed on a label, swept 37.5-43% by hand, in range). Codex p. 213 Cuba Libre build (2 oz rum, 1/4 oz lime, 4 oz cola, 3 cubes, stir 3 s, lime and cola, stir once), lime raised to 1/2 oz for the bite (Codex: lime peel is a key ingredient in most colas; the juice cuts the cola's sweetness); Joy pdf 272-273 (Baker: squeezed lime dropped in) gives the shell; Regan's 'at least one ounce' runs OUT on acid. Two dashes Angostura on top last (made in Trinidad, Codex p. 14; Oxford pdf 114). Matrix consulted, set aside (Citrus pdf 80 surprises sage, caraway, peanut, pecan: sage and caraway are sibling sparks, nuts would add a veto; Cane syrup pdf 240 surprises garlic, fish, olive). Cola reclassified nuts (safe side, C1-C2).
